nodes.body: **[info/documentation]** This comment block now claims "Every source is already provider-appropriate" — but per the PR's own summary, `ANS_LLM_API_KEY` is an explicit override that is *not* provider-bound (the binding guard covers the file layers, not the env override). The preceding sentence contradicts it two lines later ("ANS_LLM_API_KEY is an explicit override"). Worth tightening so the reasoning doesn't read as an unverified security guarantee.

**[info/documentation]** The documented order is missing a layer: `resolveLlmConfig` actually resolves `ANS_LLM_API_KEY > [llm].env_key > the provider's own env var (e.g. GEMINI_API_KEY) > the credential file`. Comment drift on the security-relevant precedence chain is what misleads later debugging.

```suggestion
// is ANS_LLM_API_KEY > [llm].env_key > the provider's own env var > the credential file.
```

**[info/maintainability]** This arrow wrapper just forwards its argument — the option type is `(env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv) => ResolvedSearchCredentials`, so the function reference works: `searchCredentials: resolveSearchCredentials`. The wrapper adds nothing and hides the actual call site.

```suggestion
searchCredentials: resolveSearchCredentials,
```

**[major/bug]** This drops the ESC byte but keeps the printable payload of a bracketed-paste marker. A real terminal paste of a key arrives as `\x1b[200~<key>\x1b[201~`; the ESC bytes are stripped, but the literal `[200~` / `[201~` remain and get concatenated into the stored key. `cleanSecret` only rejects empty/`\r\n`/control chars, so `[200~sk-...` is accepted and written — the key silently becomes wrong and later auth fails with no hint. Strip the `[200~`/`[201~` markers (or track paste state) before appending characters.

**[minor/maintainability]** Four-level nested ternary violates the no-nested-ternary rule and is hard to follow — especially since this is the logic that fixes the source-attribution ambiguity. `sources.apiKey` is a small union (`"env" | "user" | "credentials" | undefined`), so use a lookup keyed on it (with the `env` case handling the ANS_LLM_API_KEY vs provider-var distinction) instead of a chained ternary.

**[minor/bug]** Two issues in one parse: (1) `args[++i]` accepts any following token, so `ans auth set openai --endpoint --foo` silently consumes `--foo` as the URL; guard that the next token isn't another flag. (2) `--endpoint=` (empty value) is normalized to `null`, silently falling back to the default endpoint instead of erroring — the user's intent is dropped with no message. Reject empty values explicitly.

**[info/maintainability]** `@anysearch-cli/store` is already imported statically at the top of this file (lines 5 and 7). This dynamic `import()` adds nothing and obscures that the symbols are always available — move `userCredentialsPath` and `readUserCredentials` into the static import instead.

**[minor/bug]** `stored` is still computed for every provider even when `set` is already true — that's a wasted credential-file read per provider (see confirmed finding #4; hoisting the read once fixes both). More importantly, in the `show` branch the `label` logic never consults `cfg.sources.apiKey`, so a key that came from the credential file for the *selected* provider shows `AUTH` only via `name === cfg.provider && !!cfg.apiKey`; but for a non-selected provider whose stored entry is bound to a different endpoint it prints `AUTH (stored)` and then contradicts itself on the next line with "the effective endpoint differs". Pick one story: if a stored entry exists but is not effective, the label should reflect that (e.g. `NO KEY (stored for other endpoint)`) rather than claiming AUTH.

**[info/maintainability]** `ans llm check` only reports `[ERROR] ...` per provider and the old `keySet` line was the only hint; but note the `set` subcommand prints `"Make sure the SDK is installed and API key is set."` — now that a stored key is a first-class source, that hint should also mention `ans auth set <provider>`, otherwise a user who stored a key still gets told to "set an API key" with no pointer. Minor, but the message is now misleading.

**[info/maintainability]** In the `check` branch, `apiKey` here means "the canonical env var name" — the variable name collides with the concept of the resolved secret and reads confusingly next to `fromStore`/`effective`. Consider `envVarName` for clarity. (Not blocking.)

**[minor/maintainability]** The comment now lists step 3 (the provider's own env var) in a way that reads like an added layer, but the code change is only plumbing. The real new risk in this file is the session cache: `keyHash` is derived from `cfg.apiKey`, so the first `ans_chat` call after the server starts pins the slot to whatever the credential file held at that moment. `ans auth remove <provider>` / `ans auth set` on a running MCP server will produce a different `keyHash` on the next call, so the slot rebuilds — that path is covered. But if `ans auth remove` leaves `cfg.apiKey` undefined while a cached slot from a *previous different* key is still in `sessionCache`, the new key becomes `""` and `cached.keyHash === ""` never matches a previously-hashed entry, so the cache effectively stores one stale session keyed by the old provider/model/baseUrl. Confirm `state.ansChatSessionCache` is bounded, otherwise a rotation loop (credential file rewritten by an external process) inflates the Map forever, since entries are only deleted on a failed build. Add a test that rotates the credential file twice while the server stays up.

**[info/maintainability]** `db.ts` is the only CLI entry that wires `searchCredentials`; the sibling MCP entry (`apps/mcp/src/server.ts:65`) does the same thing via a redundant arrow wrapper (already flagged). Nothing to change in `db.ts` beyond the wrapper noted in the confirmed findings — just confirming the wiring matches `createEngine`'s `searchCredentials?: (env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv) => ResolvedSearchCredentials` signature, which it does.

**[minor/maintainability]** `env` is computed (`const env = opts?.env ?? process.env`) solely to feed `searchCredentials`, but the value is never used anywhere else in `createEngine` — `dbPath` still comes from `opts.dbPath`, and the domains chain uses `process.env` via `defaultDomainsDirs()`. The `env` option's doc comment claims it is "for the search-credential resolution and the db path", which is wrong on both counts (db path is `opts.dbPath`), and passing `env` with no `searchCredentials` silently does nothing. Drop the misleading clause, or wire `env` into the paths that actually read it.

**[info/maintainability]** `credentialSources` is always an object, so a consumer cannot distinguish "no search-credential resolution was configured" from "resolution ran and every arm had no key" — both look like `{}` / partial object. Since the field is declared optional, callers that want to say "this arm had no key at all" versus "we never looked" need that distinction. Return `undefined` when `searchCredentials` was not supplied (or at least when no source is recorded).

**[info/test]** `flags` here is the DACL's *control* flags (P/AI/etc.), not the ACE inheritance flags — each ACE gets its own flags field, which the loop below checks via `ace.flags.includes("I")`. That part is correct. But the test at credentials.test.ts:329 asserts `/inherits permissions|inherited entry/`; in the `/inheritance:e` case the SDDL usually keeps a `P`-less DACL and the inherited ACEs will also carry `I`, so that passes. Verify with one real Windows run that the `P` check actually fires on a truly unprotected DACL (e.g. a fresh file in a temp dir with no ACL replacement), because if `parseAces` ever picks a wrong line from `icacls /save` output the verification silently passes. No code change required — just confirm coverage of the "no P flag" branch specifically, since the current tests only hit the other two throw paths.

**[minor/maintainability]** When more than one endpoint is stored for the same provider, `forProvider[0]` is whichever entry happens to appear first in the file (sorted by endpoint in `serialize`, so lexicographically first). The resulting warning in `resolveLlmConfig` then tells the user the stored key is bound to an arbitrary endpoint. Either pick deterministically and document it, or (better) report all stored endpoints so the message is honest. Also, deleting the "wrong" entry via `ans auth remove <provider>` without `--endpoint` won't help here since the user is told to re-run `set` — consider making the message mention `ans auth list` instead of silently pointing at one endpoint.
**[info/other]** placeholder

**[major/test]** Hardcoding the credential path as `$HOME/.anysearch-cli/credentials.json` couples the test to one resolution strategy. If `credentials.ts` actually resolves the dir via `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`APPDATA` (or any path helper), `existsSync(credPath)` will be false and every downstream protection assertion (mode 600, file header markers) silently no-ops instead of failing, so the lane can go green while never checking the real file. Either derive the path the same way the product does, or assert it against the path printed by `ans auth list`/`doctor` rather than a re-typed literal.

**[major/security]** The failure detail dumps the raw `Authorization` header into `check()` output, i.e. the plaintext key appears in the very lane that asserts "no output contains the key". Any red run leaks the secret into console/CI logs. Redact before printing — e.g. map to `r.authorization?.startsWith("Bearer " + credKey) ? "Bearer <stored>" : r.authorization` or just compare booleans. Same problem in the MCP branch below with `mcpCredCalls`.

```suggestion
check(credCalls.length > 0 && credCalls.every((r) => r.authorization === "Bearer " + credKey),
        "上游收到的正是文件里那把 key（看 Authorization 头）",
        JSON.stringify(credCalls.map(() => "<redacted>")));
```

**[major/security]** Same leak: raw `authorization` values get stringified into the failure message. Redact like the CLI branch.

```suggestion
check(mcpCredCalls.length > 0 && mcpCredCalls.every((r) => r.authorization === "Bearer " + credKey),
        "MCP 的上游请求带的是同一把存起来的 key",
        JSON.stringify(mcpCredCalls.map(() => "<redacted>")));
```

**[info/test]** Non-zero exit alone is ambiguous here — a CLI that crashes for any reason (bad args, missing binary path) also yields non-zero, so this doesn't prove the "cannot protect → refuse to write" path specifically. Consider asserting on the error surface (e.g. the stderr mentions permission/protection failure) in addition to the exit code.

**被拒绝的密钥又被取回**。用户配置把 `env_key = "OPENAI_API_KEY"` 绑定到地址 A，环境中的 `ANS_LLM_BASE_URL` 改成地址 B 时，前面会拒绝这把密钥，但这里又从同一个 `OPENAI_API_KEY` 取回它。CLI 和 MCP 随后会把它交给地址 B。请记住已被绑定检查拒绝的来源，避免后续回退重新启用它，并补上规范变量名的端点切换测试。 **How this was verified:** 用户配置中的端点检查会拒绝该密钥，但后续按服务商读取环境变量时再次赋给 `apiKey`，调用方会把它和新地址一起传入模型客户端。

**地址中的秘密会被打印**。`--endpoint` 允许地址带用户名、密码或查询参数，但这里直接把原值写到终端。例如 `https://gw.example/v1?api_key=secret` 会连同密钥一起显示。`remove` 的输出和配置解析器的端点告警也有同样问题；`storedBindings` 还会把原地址交给 `ans llm` 打印。请让所有展示路径统一调用已有的 `displayEndpoint`，而不是只保护列表。 **How this was verified:** 端点只经过空白和末尾斜杠清理，随后直接拼入输出；已有的 `displayEndpoint` 才会移除用户名、密码和查询参数。
**坏记录会被静默覆盖**。有效 JSON 中只要有一条记录缺少 `apiKey`，这里就会直接丢掉它，却不设置 `error`。随后为另一家录入或删除密钥，会把过滤后的内容写回文件，永久抹掉原记录。非字符串的 `endpoint` 还会被改成默认端点。请逐条检查记录格式；发现坏记录就返回错误并拒绝改写，保持现有的坏文件保护承诺。
**并行保存会丢密钥**。两个进程同时执行 `ans auth set` 时，都可能先读到同一份旧文件，各自追加一条后再整份替换。最后完成的进程会覆盖另一条刚保存的密钥，两个命令却都报成功。保存与删除并行时也可能让已删密钥重新出现。请用跨进程锁保护整个读取、修改、写回过程，并让删除使用同一把锁；只保证重命名完整还不够。
**删除失败仍报成功**。删除最后一条记录时，这里吞掉了所有 `unlinkSync` 错误。目录没有写权限或文件无法删除时，命令仍返回成功并显示已移除，但后续 CLI 和 MCP 还会读到这把密钥。请只把文件已不存在的错误当作成功，其他错误应向上传出。

**读写使用不同主目录**。`resolveConfigHome` 在所有平台都优先选 `USERPROFILE`，但凭据和模型配置的写入仍默认用 `homedir()`。在同时有不同 `HOME`、`USERPROFILE` 的 POSIX 环境中，`ans auth set` 和 `ans llm set` 会写到一个目录，解析器却去另一个目录找，保存后仍显示缺少配置或密钥。请让读、写、删除和路径展示使用同一套目录规则，并按平台处理 `USERPROFILE`。
**方向键会混进密钥**。终端输入时这里只丢掉 ESC 字节，方向键后面的 `[D` 等字符仍会被追加到密钥里；带粘贴标记的输入同样会留下 `[200~` 和 `[201~`。这些都是可打印字符，能通过 `cleanSecret`，最终保存成功但认证失败。请完整识别并跳过转义序列，保留真正的粘贴内容，并补上终端分支测试。

`resolved.warnings` falls back to whatever the resolver produced, which includes the reason-only strings. But `resolveSearchCredentials()` already reuses the `readUserCredentials()` error, so a broken file produces the same fault twice: once at line 120 (`[FAIL] user credential file`) and again here (`[FAIL] <path>: not valid JSON …; continuing without…`). Counting one fault twice inflates `failed` and the exit summary. Skip warnings that repeat `file.error`.

**Suggestion:**

```suggestion
      if (file.error && warning.includes(file.error)) continue;
      check("  " + warning.replace(/^\[credentials\]\s*/, ""), false);
    }
```

If the paste never delivers the closing `ESC[201~` (paste cancelled, terminal quirk, or any escape sequence swallowed while `inPaste` is true), `inPaste` stays true forever and every following `\r`/`\n` is dropped. Enter never submits, so the read only ends when stdin closes, and then it throws instead of returning the pasted key. `inPaste` needs a way out — at minimum, a lone `\r` should end the read rather than be discarded.

**Suggestion:**
```suggestion
        if (ch === "\r" || ch === "\n") {
          // A newline inside a paste must not end the read half-way, but a lone
          // newline after a paste that never closed means the user pressed Enter.
          if (inPaste && !marker) {
            continue;
          }
          output.write("\n");
          return value;
        }
```

When the user file binds `base_url` but the effective provider is missing/`undefined` (e.g. only `env_key` is set in the user file and no provider layer picks one), `endpointBoundElsewhere` is true and the env_key is refused. Then line 315 (`if (!resolved.apiKey && resolved.provider)`) skips the provider-env fallback, and the credential-file lookup returns `absent` because `provider` is undefined. Result: the user's own typeable `env_key` is silently dropped although nothing was misrouted. The guard should only fire when there's an effective provider to compare against, i.e. require `resolved.provider !== undefined` here too.

**Suggestion:**
